title: Let My People Go
subtitle: The story of a burning bush, a stubborn king and a very froggy palace

scenes.title: The Burning Bush
beats: Moses grew up and became a shepherd. One day he saw something amazing: a bush on fire — but it didn’t burn up!
God spoke from the bush: “Moses! Take off your sandals — this is holy ground. I have seen My people suffering. Go to Pharaoh, and bring My people out of Egypt.”
“But who am I?” said Moses. And God answered, “I will be with you.”

scenes.title: The Staff and the Snake
beats: “But what if they don’t believe me?” Moses asked. “What is that in your hand?” said God. “A staff,” said Moses.
“Throw it on the ground.” So Moses threw it down — and it turned into a snake! Moses jumped back.
“Now pick it up by the tail,” said God. Moses did — and it turned back into a staff!

scenes.title: Let My People Go!
beats: Moses went to Pharaoh. “God says: Let My people go!” But Pharaoh said no.
So God sent plagues on Egypt — like frogs! Frogs in the beds, frogs in the ovens, frogs on Pharaoh’s throne!
Again and again Pharaoh said no. But at last, he let God’s people go.

touch.hint: Tap to make the frogs hop

scenes.title: The First Passover
beats: God told His people to get ready. “Eat a special meal tonight, with your sandals on and your bags packed. Mark your doorposts with the blood of a lamb, and death will pass over your homes.”
That night, God kept His people safe, just as He promised. And at last Pharaoh said, “Go!”
Every year after that, God’s people remembered this night: the Passover. And one day, Jesus would come as God’s own Lamb, to rescue everyone.

questions: Moses was scared and asked, “Who am I?” What did God promise him?
Why do you think Pharaoh kept saying no?
At the first Passover, God kept His people safe. How is Jesus like the Passover lamb?

verse.text: “I will surely be with you,” God said.
